prior_findings.note: Section 13 greatly expands per-member crash/fault cases, but FI-CLOSE-01 groups all handle closes and does not specify per-syscall post-error handle validity, retry safety, remaining close sequence, lock ownership, or restart oracle. Provisioning/directory Sync cases still permit multiple outcomes without tying a unique result to each injected cut.

DB/sidecar/key/provisioning cases retain conditional outcomes such as safe quarantine versus io_uncertain instead of a fixed expected result for each create/ACL/short/full-write/Sync/identity seam. Phase-tagged counters are needed to separate failed-call effects from permitted restart recovery.
Named C1-C5 IPC schedules, lock-holder crash, bounded waits, linearization and zero-effect assertions remain present.
Native Linux and NTFS Windows execution, concrete assertions, artifacts, and fail-on-skip requirements remain present.
E2E-PILOT-01..07 preserve the future loopback/browser mapping and do not treat supervisor acceptance as classroom acceptance.
Coverage thresholds/profiles, adapter platform coverage, structured event schema, cross-process trace, and negative secret/path scans remain specified.
ID width is consistently 16-byte/128-bit with 32 lowercase hex encoding in §§2, 7, and 13.
SQLite path-only verification and its trusted-directory/same-account-excluded boundary are consistent in §§2.6, 9, and FI-OPEN-03.
